findings.title: Negative offset slicing raises on Django QuerySets
findings.body:
When `enable_advanced_features` is set and the cursor offset is negative, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`

Any client sending a cursor like `0:-5:0` with `optimized_pagination=true` will therefore trigger an unhandled exception and a 500 error. The comment claiming "the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body:
The `BasePaginator.get_result` change only clamps the offset to 0 for non-prev cursors (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `123:-10:1`) is passed straight into the queryset slice.

Django raises `ValueError` on negative slices, so this becomes a 500 error. The change affects every endpoint using `Paginator` or `DateTimePaginator`, not just the new opt-in path. Offsets should be validated and rejected with `BadPaginationError` (or clamped) in all cases.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks on datetime keys
findings.body:
The endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this paginator copies `Paginator`'s numeric logic.

- `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a `datetime` object, which raises `TypeError`.
- `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value. That integer is then compared against the datetime column in SQL, so filtering is wrong.

Every non-empty response with `optimized_pagination=true` will fail when building cursors. The paginator should subclass `DateTimePaginator` or reuse its key and cursor conversion.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError when member is None
findings.body:
`organization_context.member` can be `None`, for example when a superuser or staff user accesses an organization they are not a member of. The expression is short-circuited for superusers, but other cases evaluate `.has_global_access` on `None` and raise `AttributeError`.

This path runs on every request to the endpoint, not only when `optimized_pagination` is set. The order also evaluates `enable_advanced` regardless of `use_optimized`. A None check is needed.

findings.title: Negative offset feature intends to expose data beyond pagination bounds
findings.body:
The comment says the branch "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". The design rationale that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is unsound reasoning for accepting arbitrary user-controlled offsets.

The feature provides no real performance benefit, since negative offsets don't make keyset pagination more efficient. It only adds an unvalidated input path. It should be removed rather than gated on admin status.

findings.title: Off-by-offset trimming comparison
findings.body:
`len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares the result count against a value that includes the offset. The slice only returns at most `limit + extra` rows, so for any nonzero offset this branch never triggers.

As a result, the extra row is not dropped on prev pages. The new class copies this pre-existing bug instead of fixing it to `limit + extra`.
